caption: Key terms and meanings
rows: An explicit assumption about how observations, relations or target states arise, used to derive and test candidate model operations.
Support is the domain of admissible or empirically represented states. Coverage describes how observations occupy that domain.
A local scale summarizes nearby distances. A scale trace records that quantity across several neighbourhood sizes.
An operation that defines or scores connections between observations or entities.
An operation that produces the next state and must satisfy the target state’s structural requirements.
A local mask, distance bias or update gate that constrains attention using anchored data geometry.
The tested corrections meet their safety criteria only by suppressing useful mixing or update amplitude.
A small validation comparison used to select an operation. In the final procedure it uses training data only.
No-op retains the unchanged baseline. Abstention withholds a model choice or prediction when evidence is insufficient.
Adjustment of output probabilities to the occurrence frequencies relevant to the target population.
Used broadly for a relation or state operation. The term does not always denote a positive-semidefinite kernel function.

caption: Table 1. Hypotheses assessed across the experiments.
rows: Global attention can bridge low-density gaps and rearrange local geometry.
Gap occupancy rises by 38.2% in Breast Cancer and 117.4% in Digits. Global attention retains fewer neighbours than local attention in all four datasets.
Blocking cross-gap relations always preserves attention as a valid state-transition operator.
Across three discrete graphs, mixing adjacency rows produces non-edge mass, self-loops and asymmetry even under an observed-neighbour mask. Meeting safety thresholds requires N_eff close to 1.
Local compression scale can define a data-derived relation scale.
Elastic local distances produce repeated gains across four classification datasets and Diabetes regression, especially in sparse regions.
Adding higher-order acceleration and jerk features improves modelling.
Long spring traces, higher-order differences and enforced acceleration penalties repeatedly overfit or reduce performance.
A scale trace is more informative than one fixed local scale.
Datasets prefer different k values. Direct averaging can reduce performance; routing among scale families is more stable.
Uneven training density should always trigger inverse-density loss weighting.
Simple inverse-density weights are unstable across datasets and slightly reduce Diabetes regression performance.
Structural learning and occurrence frequency should be treated separately.
Diabetes BMI coverage balancing reduces macro-RMSE from 65.43 to 60.22 and overall RMSE from 64.01 to 63.37.
Wrapper exhaustion can guide replacement of attention aggregation.
Karate, Davis and Florentine retain state violations under admissible neighbour relations; the tested safe settings have N_eff close to 1.
A diagnostic requires interpretation under the target mechanism before selecting an action.
BMI, s4 and age respond differently to coverage balancing. Natural RMSE and macro-RMSE also support different decisions on the same data.
Structural learning can be separated from prevalence and followed by output calibration.
Balanced Digits training improves balanced accuracy and recall but raises log-loss. Prevalence calibration recovers about 80% of the additional log-loss.
Biased sampling reduces peripheral Digits accuracy from 93.13% to 86.99%; oracle inverse-propensity weighting restores it only to 87.59%.
Attention may score proposals while another operation generates admissible discrete states.
Global discrete projection restores valid graph form. Relation-only edge gating preserves observed support and symmetry; binary state generation remains a separate requirement.
Operator selection should reflect state constraints, relation order and the hypothesized mechanism.
Davis path orders 1, 2 and 4 give AUC 0.500 for missing cross-partition edges. Three hops give 0.753; degree-normalized three-hop relations give 0.806.
Insufficient relation evidence is a valid decision outcome.
Florentine candidates are weak across 100 edge-recovery splits, mostly with AUC approximately 0.43–0.60. The graph has limited cycle redundancy and clustering.
Mechanism diagnostics can directly specify the final operation before downstream results are inspected.
ModeChoice, RAND HIE and Les Misérables improve on their principal metrics. Forced coverage correction fails on Engel, favouring candidate generation followed by selection.
A diagnostic can be equated directly with an action.
Despite uneven Engel coverage, forced balancing raises macro-RMSE from 130.08 to 135.07. A nested probe chooses the unchanged model in 63 of 80 outer splits.
An unchanged baseline and abstention must be formal candidates.
The Engel probe selects ordinary training in 78.75% of outer splits and substantially reduces the loss from automatic correction.
Diagnostics should identify admissible losses and candidate families before a precise algorithm is selected.
RAND HIE deviance improves by only about 0.067% under Poisson modelling, with variance about seven times the mean. ModeChoice improves NLL while accuracy is nearly unchanged.
